question: What does G3 mean in the gate ladder — and is red-first a gate every card must pass, or an obligation cards are trusted to remember? (D-1, raised by G6 on card a4-gate-ladder: decision 140 says N/A — openspec absent; decision 101 says red-first re-verified by G6)
proposal: Give red-first its own named gate row (RF); G3 stays N/A — retire the recycled number that produced the contradiction

votes.note: Q-KR3 is graded on red-first this cycle; an obligation with no gate behind it failed 3 of 4 times last night — the KR needs the gate
a named row changes every future slate and launch prompt; ruling either way is an operator call, correctly escalated rather than legislated inside a run
the ladder already prescribes names-not-numbers for new gates; RF preserves decision 101's substance without rewriting decision 140's row

question: What backup should production have? (D-2a, raised by the 2026-08-06 incident: the dropped production database had no PITR, no dumps, and an empty alternate volume — B-143)
proposal: Nightly pg_dump outside the Docker volume now, WAL-based PITR as the follow-up

votes.note: the business lost templates, users, submissions and recipes with no restore path; restorability is table stakes before any feature work matters
the floor is an hour of work (Taskfile target + cron line) and can be built unattended; PITR is a scheduled follow-up, not a blocker
image rollback exists and data rollback does not — the asymmetry B-143 names; either half alone converts a drop into a twenty-minute restore

weighing: No adopted preferences exist to weigh (operations/C-2 is pending only). Escalated to the operator, who chose dump AND PITR — recorded as ledger §T-38 decision 154, promoted to card prod-backup-floor-and-pitr.
reasons: role pm cast an unrecognized severity "high" (want low, medium, top)
top-severity questions are the operator's — no number of citations clears them

question: Should the test suites keep sharing one Postgres cluster with production? (D-2b, raised by B-141: the RLS suite holds admin credentials to the cluster serving hq.yumyums.kitchen, and a G6 probe executed DROP DATABASE against production through them)
proposal: Separate test-only Postgres container; no test file holds admin credentials to production

votes.note: a test mistake must be structurally unable to be a production mistake; the guard-fix alternative was demonstrated insufficient by the incident itself
one more container and DSN to keep straight, against removing an entire failure class; also unblocks the hq_test_go repair question permanently
a blocklist cannot enumerate per-leg, per-environment names (B-141's mechanism); separation is an impossibility argument where a guard is only a correctness argument
